rules_text:
Rules summary Quinque official English rules Contents 1 Overview 2 Game play 2.1 Mark a skydiver 2.2 Move a tile 3 Game end 3.1 Win 3.2 Tie Overview Each player has 18 parachutes of their colour. One player places a parachute on the first tile. Players take turns to: Mark a skydiver or move a tile . Optionally move a tile . The winner is the first player to make a line of five of their parachutes. Game play Mark a skydiver Choose a free skydiver on an already-played tile and put a parachute on their back. OR Add a new tile adjacent to an already placed one and add a parachute to one of the new tile's skydivers. Move a tile Select a tile. Move the tile to any free space on a horizontal, vertical, or diagonal line. All tiles must have edge connections. A tile cannot be moved if: One of its skydivers was marked in the same turn, or The tile is surrounded on all 4 edges. Tiles may not be rotated. Advanced rules for moving tiles # Parachutes Move the tile Row or column Diagonal Through other tiles 1 adjacent position only ✔ ✘ ✘ 2 any free position ✔ ✘ ✔ 3 any free position ✘ ✔ ✔ 4 any free position ✔ ✔ ✔ Game end Win The active player immediately wins if five of their own skydivers are aligned. Horizontally, vertically, or diagonally. Tie Both players are out of parachutes.

[Rating: 4/10] Each tile has a token spot in 4 corners and the aim is to keep placing a token each turn and move a tile (the second part of each turn) until you can engineer having 5 tokens in a row. That's about it. There's nothing too clever, just keep working the problem (until someone accidentally wins), and nothing inspiring in the abstractedness of it all.

[Rating: 5/10] This is a kind of connect five with a pasted on skydiving theme. Each tile has a sky diver without a parachute in each of the four corners. On your turn, you must add a parachute to an existing skydiver without one or add a tile orthogonally adjacent to an existing one and then add a parachute to a skydiver on the newly placed tile. Then you may move a tile without rotating it. In the basic rules you just move the tile anywhere in the row, column, or diagonal, even through an existing tile, as long as it ends up orthogonally adjacent to the mass of tiles and doesn't overlap.
